provenance: PR #29 R11. R5's defect had two halves and only one was graded. `expect.planner_note_contains` reads `stub_planner.notes` — what the CALL SITE passed — and every offline case uses the stub, so the line R5 actually changed in `live_planner` is executed only by `full`-tagged cases. The reviewer demonstrated it: reverting that line to the old shared prefix left `probe3-quotes-most-quoted-author` reporting `planner_note_contains: true` and both suites green, while a real planner went back to being told 'A previous attempt failed' about a plan that never ran. The message build is now the pure function `planner.build_user`, and this case grades it directly: the note arrives verbatim, and the planner adds no framing of its own in either direction — no replan sentence when there is no note, and the lint's message does not acquire the act ladder's.

triage.note: tagged invariant AND fast: it is pure code, costs nothing measurable, and is the only thing in the repo that reads the prompt a paid run would send. It grades the assembly, not the wording — no case can say whether a given sentence makes a real model plan better, and the `full` suite is where that would be measured.
